topic: ChatGPT vs Google: How LLMs Work
description: Practical answers about retrieval vs generation, hallucinations, training vs inference, and when to trust AI outputs.

questions.question: What's the main difference between Google Search and ChatGPT?
questions.answer: Google searches its index of web pages and returns ranked links — that's retrieval. ChatGPT generates answers from patterns learned during training — that's generation. Google can say 'no results found'; ChatGPT will often generate something even when it doesn't know the answer.

questions.question: How does Google build and use its search index?
questions.answer: Google's crawlers (spiders) constantly visit websites and store content in a massive index — like a table of contents for the web. When you search, Google looks up this pre-built index instead of scanning the live internet. Ranking depends on domain authority, backlinks, page speed, keywords, and SEO factors.

questions.question: What is a base model and how is it different from ChatGPT?
questions.answer: A base model is the raw AI that only predicts the next token — like a giant autocomplete. ChatGPT is built on top with instruction tuning, safety filters, tool access, web search, and conversation management. Think: base model = engine, ChatGPT = car with all the features.

questions.question: What is an AI hallucination and how do I avoid trusting false answers?
questions.answer: Hallucination is when AI makes up information and presents it confidently as fact. It's not lying — it's predicting the next best word. To reduce risk: ask for sources, say 'only answer if you're sure', ask about uncertainties, use web search/RAG for grounding, and never trust AI alone for medical or legal advice.

questions.question: What is the difference between training and inference?
questions.answer: Training is the school phase — the AI studies massive datasets to learn patterns (expensive, done once or periodically). Inference is the working phase — every time you send a prompt, the trained model generates a response in real time. Training builds the brain; inference uses it.

questions.question: What is RAG and why is it important for real-world AI?
questions.answer: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) combines external evidence retrieval with LLM text generation. Web search + LLM = retrieval provides facts, generation gives readable answers. This is crucial for personal assistants, document Q&A, and any app where the LLM needs access to your private data or current information.

questions.question: Why do LLMs have a knowledge cutoff date?
questions.answer: Retraining on new data is complex and extremely expensive — models aren't updated daily. Each LLM is trained on data available up to a certain date (check model docs). For current events, models rely on tools like web search rather than retraining. This is why knowledge cutoff matters for factual questions about recent events.
